name: INDEVCO North America Orangeburg – DBA INDEVCO Plastics Orangeburg LLC
IRON BOND FABRICATION
old_description: Stainless process piping, food-grade equipment, structural steel and mobile
about:
Iron Bond Fabrication is a family-run welding and fabrication shop based in Springdale, Arkansas. The company operates a fabrication shop and a mobile service truck, serving plants, contractors, and property owners across Northwest Arkansas.

The shop focuses on four core areas: sanitary and food-grade welding for process piping, tanks, hoppers, and blenders used in food and beverage plants and breweries; structural steel fabrication of platforms, mezzanines, stair towers, catwalks, and equipment frames; mobile welding that brings on-site repair and fabrication to the customer's plant or job site; and custom one-off metalwork such as gates, railing, brackets, trailers, and prototypes built from drawings, photos, or rough sketches. Work is performed in a small shop facility with a service truck for field jobs.

Customers include food and beverage processors, breweries, general contractors, maintenance departments, and property owners throughout Northwest Arkansas. The company has worked with firms such as Tidey Excavation and handles projects that must accommodate production schedules, sanitation windows, and plant shutdowns.

Iron Bond emphasizes that the person who quotes a job is the person who welds it, ensuring no loss of detail between estimate and finished part. The company highlights proper fit-up, purge, and heat control on every weld, straight answers on schedule and price with early notice of changes, experience working inside operating facilities, and a policy of leaving the job site as clean as they found it.

name: ISAIC - Industrial Sewing and Innovation Center
old_description: We are dedicated to revolutionizing the textile and apparel industry through standardizing a human-centered approach to innovative manufacturing and skilling.
about:
ISAIC, the Industrial Sewing and Innovation Center, operates from Detroit, Michigan. The organization was founded in Detroit, though a specific year is not publicly disclosed. It functions as an innovation hub rather than a traditional factory, governed by a mission to standardize a human-centered approach to manufacturing and workforce development in the textile and apparel sector.

The center focuses on innovative manufacturing practices and skilling programs, running innovation pilots and training people both at its Detroit facility and nationally. It maintains a network of local partners and licensees, though specific facility size, headcount, or production volumes are not disclosed. Its work emphasizes integrating people and technology to advance processes and practices.

ISAIC serves the textile and apparel industry, engaging with donors, partners, investors, and licensees who support its mission. Its model appears designed to transform the sector through collaborative innovation rather than direct contract manufacturing for external clients.

The organization distinguishes itself by centering human capital alongside technology, aiming to create a standardized, replicable framework for modern apparel manufacturing. Its founding premise is that sustainable industry transformation requires investing in people as much as in equipment.

name: ISCA Hygienic Processing Solutions
old_description: ISCA is a leading provider of industry-proven equipment solutions to the Meat, Bakery and wider food industry.
about:
ISCA Hygienic Processing Solutions operates from Bethesda, Maryland. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed. It began as a provider of equipment solutions for the meat, bakery, and broader food processing sectors, building a team that collectively holds over 200 years of food manufacturing experience.

The firm supplies both new and used machinery, acting as an authorized agent for several global manufacturers of meat and bakery equipment. Through its engineering division, ISCA also produces its own line of ancillary support equipment and offers refurbishment and customization services to match customer specifications. The company maintains an inventory of hundreds of machines available for next-day dispatch.

ISCA serves a wide range of food sectors including meat, bakery, pet food, snack food, poultry, prepared foods, seafood, dairy, chocolate, frozen foods, and beverages, as well as pharmaceutical, cannabis, and cosmetic production. Its customer base spans start-ups, mid-market producers, and large industrial operations, with services covering facility build-outs, efficiency upgrades, and compliance-driven projects.

The company states its goal is to form lifetime partnerships, operating on the principle that helping clients grow drives its own growth. It assists with establishing and scaling new ventures, improving efficiency and compliance for existing plants, and delivering customized systems for handling, processing, packaging, hygiene, and washing.

name: Idaho Manufacturing Alliance
old_description: The Voice of Idaho Manufacturers  --  Powering a $22.5 Billion Industry
about:
The Idaho Manufacturing Alliance (IMA) operates from Nampa, Idaho. It was founded in the fall of 2013 as the Southwest Idaho Manufacturers' Alliance (SWIMA) by a group of local manufacturing executives and economic development representatives who recognized the distinct challenges and opportunities facing manufacturers in the region. The organization began hosting events in 2014 and launched official membership in December 2014. In 2021, SWIMA rebranded as the Idaho Manufacturing Alliance to expand its impact statewide.

IMA serves as a member organization representing Idaho's manufacturing sector, uniting more than 200 member companies that collectively represent approximately 2,200 manufacturers and a $21.5 billion industry. The alliance focuses on three pillars: connecting manufacturers through events, training, and networking; supporting the sector with workforce development, talent pipeline initiatives, and sourcing assistance; and promoting the industry by advocating for favorable policies and raising public awareness of manufacturing careers.

The organization's members span the breadth of Idaho's manufacturing base, including supply chain partners, business advisors, and strategic partners.

IMA was created by manufacturers, for manufacturers, with a mission to nurture an environment of knowledge sharing, innovation, and sustainable growth. Its core values emphasize passion for the industry, advocacy through collaboration, dedication to authenticity and service, and building awareness through knowledge sharing.

name: Ideal Fabricators Inc
old_description: We provide heavy steel plate fabricating, large CNC machining, and precision plate burning. Located in Michigan, Ideal Fabricators and Statewide Boring proudly serves all of North America.
about:
Ideal Fabricators Inc. operates from Livonia, Michigan, where it was founded in 1984 by Patrick Purdom to serve the machine tool industry across the state. The company expanded its plant and crane capacity in 1998 to handle larger fabrications and reach customers beyond Michigan. In 2003 it partnered with Statewide Boring & Machine to offer complete fabricated and machined parts throughout North America, and Statewide Boring more than doubled its plant footprint in 2011 to accommodate new CNC equipment. In 2022 the business transitioned to 100 percent employee ownership.

The shop provides heavy steel plate fabrication, large CNC machining, precision plate burning, and heat-treat and straightening services. Its expanded facilities allow end-to-end production so that a single purchase order can cover fabrication, machining, laser inspection, and finish painting. The combination of plate burning, machining, and finishing under one roof is intended to reduce lead times and coordinate quality control across operations.

While the original customer base was the Michigan machine tool sector, the company now ships to manufacturers across the United States and Canada. Projects shown in its gallery include structural frames, base plates, and machined components for industrial equipment builders and OEMs in sectors such as heavy machinery, energy, and transportation.

The firm emphasizes that consolidating fabrication, machining, inspection, and coating into one workflow eliminates handoffs between vendors and shortens overall project schedules. Employee ownership, adopted in 2022, is presented as a further alignment of workforce incentives with on-time delivery and part quality.
